trial_court: MM (Magistrate's Court) and ASJ (Additional Sessions Judge)
case_name: Smt. Sushila Sharma vs Anil Kumar Sharma
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a complaint under Section 494 of the IPC against respondent for solemnizing another marriage during subsistence of first marriage. Trial court acquitted respondent. Petitioner alleges she came to know about second marriage through mother-in-law.

legal_principles.principle: A party who fails to avail of opportunities granted by the court does not deserve any further opportunity.
legal_principles.held: The trial court observed that she does not deserve any opportunity. The court dismissed her application of waiver of cost of Rs. 1,000/- and also closed her post charge evidence.
cited_cases: Smt. Sushila Sharma vs Anil Kumar Sharma on 13 March, 2020

legal_principles.principle: A party must take steps to summon witnesses as directed by the court.
legal_principles.held: The appellant was directed to summon her remaining witnesses on 17.07.2017. Since the petitioner had not taken steps for summoning of the witnesses for 17.07.2017, cost of Rs. 1,000/- was imposed upon her and she was directed to summon all the witnesses for the next date of hearing i.e 08.09.2017.
cited_cases: Smt. Sushila Sharma vs Anil Kumar Sharma on 13 March, 2020

outcome.final_order: Trial court's decision upheld, no evidence found to establish respondent had solemnized another marriage during subsistence of first marriage.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation
preparing a complaint for bigamy and criminal harassment
